intent: Synthetic example of a surgical cinematic edit: fracture the moon while preserving the existing cyber-city live-action frame.

inputs.description: User-supplied source frame containing an intact moon in the upper-left sky. This packaged example does not include the actual image.

scene.summary: A grounded live-action night view of a dense near-future city beneath a large moon.
scene.setting: High-rise urban skyline with restrained cybernetic infrastructure and atmospheric haze.

subjects.description: The existing lunar disk, changed into a physically fractured celestial body with separated crustal plates and deep internal fissures.
appearance: subtle cold internal light inside the deepest fissures
subjects.action: Breaking apart slowly without exploding outward.
subjects.pose: Existing circular silhouette remains broadly readable.
subjects.scale: Preserve the apparent diameter of the original moon.
relationships: Do not overlap or displace buildings.
Match the existing haze and atmospheric perspective.

composition.framing: Preserve every crop boundary and the moon's center position.
composition.negative_space: Preserve the existing sky around the moon.

lighting.summary: Integrate the fracture into the source exposure without relighting the city.
lighting.rim: no new rim light on the skyline

materials.description: Dry cratered rock with massive crustal slabs, powdery regolith edges, deep shadowed gaps, and physically credible debris scale.

optics.motion_blur: No added camera blur; minimal slow debris motion only.
optics.lens_character: Match source lens and atmospheric response.

spatial_edits.instruction: Transform only the intact lunar disk into a physically fractured moon. Preserve its center, apparent diameter, broad silhouette, atmospheric depth, and surrounding sky. The moon is splitting into a few massive rocky plates with deep irregular fissures; it is not a fiery explosion.

must_preserve: all skyline geometry and building placement
moon center at x 16.5 percent and y 16.4 percent
source exposure, color grade, haze, grain, and lens response
all pixels outside the approximate lunar edit region as closely as the editor permits
must_change: only the intact lunar disk becomes physically fractured

quality_controls: preserve only source-motivated grain, halation, bloom, and optical artifacts
